findings.claim: gc-05 used Kombu's 3600-second Redis visibility default while late-ack tasks and the configured FFmpeg interval can run for 86400 seconds.
findings.source: gc-05 deployed Celery/Kombu runtime probe; lx_annotate/settings/settings_base.py; endoreg_db/tasks.py

findings.claim: The production-safe value is 90000 seconds, exported identically as CELERY_VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT, broker transport visibility_timeout, and result transport visibility_timeout, with a one-hour margin over every configured late-ack task.
findings.source: Celery Redis transport contract and gc-05 task/runtime timeout inventory

findings.claim: The missing implicit route for endoreg_db.tasks.video_hls_materialization must target ffmpeg_media.
All workers consuming Redis DB 1 must restart together after deployment because the shortest visibility timeout used by a shared broker wins.
findings.source: Celery Redis documentation and gc-05 worker topology

gaps: A 25-hour behavioral redelivery test is not practical before today's user session; effective live Kombu channel and worker configuration must be inspected immediately after deployment.
The separate explicit HLS task hard limit remains shorter than the host's maximum FFmpeg interval.
